clue.text: Cabal swindles with copy-right-breaking

parts.note: to con someone is to swindle them, so swindles are cons
piracy is the infringement of copyright, as with pirated books or recordings

explanation.surface: A secret group rips people off by flouting copyright.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a secret faction, and a plot hatched by such a group is a conspiracy; the words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Ship's company were exultant

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is celebrating.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's sailors form its crew, and crew is also an old past tense of crow, to exult or boast.

clue.text: Stick up the French, somebody

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for stick is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a baton is a short stick, as carried by a conductor or relay runner
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A robbery is being held up by the French, by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction, a somebody rather than a nobody.

clue.text: For every arrival on a river, perhaps

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Every time something arrives on a river, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' just means placed above the next piece, so it joins rather than signals an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic adverb meaning by chance or possibly, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Note something done and the response

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
an action is a deed, something that has been done

explanation.surface: Write down what happened and how people answered.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is the reply or reflex answer provoked by something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Disagreement about a woman's old hood

indicators.note: about means the word for disagreement goes around the letter from the clue

parts.note: a clash is a conflict or disagreement

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerning a lady's antique headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A calash was a large folding silk hood worn by women in the eighteenth century, named after the hooded carriage.

clue.text: Girl has a happy event

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman is throwing a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration, a joyful public event.

clue.text: Put on a very quiet German number

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
a lied is a German art song, a musical number

explanation.surface: A German song is performed very softly.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint or ointment that is applied has been put on a surface, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: What the aged, first and last, may plead

definitions.text: What the aged, first and last, may plead

parts.words: What the aged, first and last, may plead
parts.note: the old blame their years for their failings; the Latin phrase for in the year of the Lord is a jokey name for old age, and its initials are a first and last letter

explanation.surface: Elderly people offer an excuse from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Anno Domini is jocular for advancing age, so the old 'plead' it as an excuse; 'first and last' hints at its abbreviation AD, the first and last letters of AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase dating the Christian era is used humorously to mean old age, the excuse of the elderly.

clue.text: One-time bird marble, viewed from outside

parts.note: ex means former or one-time, as in ex-wife
the tern is a seabird
an ally is a choice glass or alabaster marble used in the children's game

explanation.surface: A former bird and a marble, seen from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen externally is regarded from the outside, so the adverb matches the phrase.

clue.text: A lifetime of bridge

explanation.surface: A whole life spent playing a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a stretch of time such as one's life span, and to span a river is to bridge it.

clue.text: Useful when calling on the odd bod?

definitions.text: Useful when calling on the odd bod?

parts.words: Useful when calling on the odd bod?
parts.note: calling here means paying a social visit, and the odd bod is just any person you drop in on

explanation.surface: Something handy when you phone a strange fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' suggests a phone call; here it means paying a visit, when one left a small printed card with one's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A visiting-card is a small printed card bearing one's name, left when making a social call.

clue.text: "Gentlemen in England, now " (Henry V)

parts.note: the King's St Crispin's Day speech goes on to say these gentlemen will think themselves accursed they were not at Agincourt

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank line from Shakespeare's history play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Henry V's Agincourt speech the stay-at-home gentlemen of England are pictured as still in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means in bed, as the gentlemen in England were while the battle was fought.

clue.text: Declared if I tried 9

indicators.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 9 across, meaning outside, so the word for tried sits around the clue's if I

parts.note: to test something is to try it, so tried gives tested

explanation.surface: Stated that one would have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: The '9' points to 9 across, EXTERNALLY: TESTED goes outside IFI.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence or affirm under oath, so testified means formally stated.

clue.text: Not as one pair possibly desire

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A couple might not want to be counted as a single unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NOT, AS, I (one) and PAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a hope or ambition, something longed for.

clue.text: Such a key held by John, the poet?

definitions.text: Such a key held by John, the poet?

indicators.note: held by means the key letter is gripped inside the poet's surname

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor poet, tutor to the young Henry VIII
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A master key belonging to John, the writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is both definition and wordplay: a skeleton key, and the key E inside SKELTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key is a master key filed down to open many locks.

clue.text: Job shows its price is above rubies

definitions.text: Job shows its price is above rubies

parts.words: Job shows its price is above rubies
parts.note: the Book of Job, chapter 28, says the price of a certain quality is above rubies

explanation.surface: A particular job reveals what it is worth: more than precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work; it is the Old Testament book, where this quality is priced above rubies.
explanation.definitionFit: Job 28:18 says the value of sound judgement and knowledge is greater than that of rubies.

clue.text: Vessel maybe then to get lighter

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word then could appear in another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship might then be relieved of its load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal; 'lighter' looks like a small boat beside 'Vessel' but means brighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To brighten is to become lighter or more luminous, as the sky does at dawn.

clue.text: Egg? Usually nice surroundings for it

indicators.note: surroundings for means the jumbled letters enclose the little word that follows
usually here suggests the word nice taken in an unusual arrangement, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An egg usually has pleasant surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Usually' is a loose anagram signal on 'nice', and 'Egg' is a verb, as in egg on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or provoke them, the same as to incite.

clue.text: An apple for Shakespeare's clown

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit belonging to a comic character in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A costard is a large English cooking apple, and Costard is the clown in Love's Labour's Lost.

clue.text: What earth produces a particle of enjoyment

parts.note: the soil yields crops, its fruit
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: The soil yields a little bit of pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruition originally meant the pleasure of possessing or using something, an old sense of enjoyment.

clue.text: Batting to play for time when put in

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is in
to stall is to delay or play for time

explanation.surface: A batsman tries to waste time when sent in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To install equipment is to put it in place, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Severity of our costume for a start

indicators.note: for a start means the costume word comes first, ahead of our

parts.note: a rig is an outfit or costume, as in rig-out

explanation.surface: Our harsh outfit to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour is strictness or harshness, as in the rigour of the law.

clue.text: Carol follows Jack round the globe — imbibing?

indicators.note: follows puts the carol after the sailor

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: round means the singing word is wrapped around the globe word

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
an orb is a sphere or globe

explanation.surface: A carol is sung after Jack sails round the world, while drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman; 'round' wraps the carol around the globe, and 'follows' puts that after the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbing means soaking up or drinking in, so it matches taking in liquid.

clue.text: Blow the taste of the old-fashioned!

explanation.surface: Down with the preferences of the fuddy-duddies!
explanation.definitionFit: A gust is a blast of wind, and in archaic English gust also meant relish or taste, from Latin gustus.

clue.text: Divine, in either of two Scandinavian books

definitions.text: Divine, in either of two Scandinavian books

parts.words: Divine, in either of two Scandinavian books
parts.note: both Old Norse collections, the Elder and the Younger, are full of the stories of the gods

explanation.surface: Something holy appears in one of a pair of Norse volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the Poetic and the Prose works of this name tell the myths of the Norse gods, hence 'Divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is the name of two Old Icelandic books of Norse mythology and poetry, the Elder and the Younger.

clue.text: The Italian mother of a Muslim leader

parts.note: i is an Italian plural form of the
mam is a dialect word for mother

explanation.surface: The Italian mother of a man who leads Muslims.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads prayers in a mosque, or a Muslim spiritual leader.

clue.text: Against the company's illegal traffic

parts.note: contra is Latin for against, as in pros and contras
a band is a company of people or musicians

explanation.surface: Opposing the firm's unlawful trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband is smuggled goods or the trade in them, unlawful commerce.

clue.text: An idea covering a brood of pheasants

indicators.note: covering means the letters lie within the words an idea

explanation.surface: A notion takes in a nest of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A nide is the collective noun for a nest or brood of pheasants.

clue.text: Passion-fruit makes us sick in a Spanish city

indicators.note: in means the word for sick is placed inside the city name

parts.note: Granada is a city in Andalusia, home of the Alhambra
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Tropical fruit upsets our stomachs in an Andalusian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A granadilla is the fruit of a passion-flower, a variety of passion-fruit.
